title: Unsupervised Generative Feature Transformation via Graph Contrastive Pre-training and Multi-objective Fine-tuning

problem.claim: Feature transformation must derive new features from original features, but in science domains supervised labels may require expensive and lengthy experiments.

gap.claim: Existing methods rely on domain knowledge or expensive supervised feedback, face large search spaces, or overlook nonlinear feature interactions; an unsupervised paradigm is needed to capture complex interactions while avoiding large search spaces.

contributions.claim: A feature value consistency preservation perspective and a mean discounted cumulative gain-like unsupervised metric are developed to evaluate feature set utility.
An unsupervised graph contrastive learning encoder is developed to represent feature sets as feature-feature interaction graphs.

A deep generative feature transformation model is developed to generate feature transformations from feature-cross sequences while coordinating a pretrained encoder with utility-evaluator gradient information.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating the effectiveness, efficiency, traceability, and explicitness of the framework.

narrative_sequence.summary: Feature transformation augments data by deriving new features, while supervised labels in some scientific applications are costly to obtain.
These costs motivate unsupervised feature transformation learning, which must handle complex interactions without a large search space.
Existing approaches have limitations involving domain knowledge, supervised feedback, search-space size, or nonlinear interactions.
The framework measures feature-set utility, pretrains graph-based representations contrastively, and fine-tunes a generative transformation model using utility gradients.
The authors report extensive experiments evaluating the framework's effectiveness, efficiency, traceability, and explicitness.
